title: Data Models and Storage Engines
focus: Derive logical and physical data models from quantified access paths, invariants, retention, growth, and ownership.

pacing.review: Skim lessons, answer self-checks, and take one generated quiz.
pacing.standard: Study lessons, complete guided practice, use the answer key, and take one or more generated quizzes.
pacing.deep: Complete standard work plus the reinforcement lab and optional project.

lessons.title: Workloads, Access Paths, and Data Models
Pages, Records, Buffer Pools, and Locality
B+ Trees, Hash Indexes, and Inverted Indexes
LSM Paths, Bloom Filters, Tombstones, and Compaction
Query Plans, Statistics, and Index Design
Skew, Background Debt, Stalls, and Diagnosis
Storage Decisions, Migration, Cost, and Ownership

learning_outcomes.statement: Derive logical and physical data models from quantified access paths, invariants, retention, growth, and ownership.
Explain and measure how pages, records, buffer pools, locality, and cache policy shape physical work.
Implement and validate a persistent paged B+ tree with point lookup, range scan, splits, cache behavior, deletion, and clean reopen.
Implement and validate an LSM store with memtable, SSTables, sparse indexes, Bloom filters, tombstones, and compaction.
Calculate read, write, and space amplification and connect them to tail latency, capacity, cost, and SSD endurance.
Choose indexes and diagnose query plans whose estimates, statistics, or access paths do not match the workload.
Diagnose read, write, range, skew, delete, cache, Bloom, compaction, and tombstone behavior from preserved same-input evidence.
Defend a storage-engine decision covering security, operations, cost, ownership, migration, rollback, recovery requirements, and reversal evidence.

lab.note: Use the lab to reinforce the local mechanism; treat expanded matrices and platform-specific evidence as optional deep-dive work.

optional_project.description: Apply Data Models and Storage Engines to a small system you know. Write a short design note, experiment report, or implementation summary only if you want deeper practice.
